trust_decision.summary: Which websocket clients receive a role_updated event (carrying the role's full permission JSON) is decided in App.sendUpdatedRoleEvent, which at the pinned commit publishes with empty team/channel/user, i.e. to every connected user, even for team- or channel-scheme roles.

landing_point.why: The summary names the role_updated websocket event; grepping WebsocketEventRoleUpdated leads straight to sendUpdatedRoleEvent, its only publisher.

fix_sites.entry_point: PUT /api/v4/roles/{role_id}/patch (server/channels/api4/role.go:28,224) -> App.PatchRole; PUT /api/v4/channels/{channel_id}/moderations/patch (server/channels/api4/channel.go:84,2359); bulk import role/scheme lines (server/channels/app/import.go:356 -> import_functions.go:169 UpdateRole cascade); shared-channel readonly moderation (server/platform/services/sharedchannel/service.go:263)
POST /api/v4/schemes and channel moderation patch creating a channel scheme (server/channels/app/channel.go:751) -> store createScheme; now records SchemeId on every scheme role (fix.diff:680-777)
internal: role Save/Get/GetByNames/AllChannelSchemeRoles/ChannelRolesUnderTeamRole mapping the new SchemeId column (fix.diff:576-672)
public model: Role struct JSON/YAML/Auditable gain scheme_id (fix.diff:1031-1076)
DB migrations 000142-000144 (add Roles.SchemeId, backfill from Schemes.Default*Role, index), run at server start

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: server/channels/store/sqlstore/scheme_store.go:102 (createScheme assigns scheme.Id only at :283, after roles are created; fix moves it up and stamps SchemeId on each role, fix.diff:680-777) plus migrations fix.diff:394-571

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The cascade at server/channels/app/role.go:243-250 re-emits events for other roles after a system/team role change, which a solver can call 'propagation of an admin-wide change' and leave global, while scoping only the channel-moderation caller that already has channel.Id at server/channels/app/channel.go:1111.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Built-in and scheme-less custom roles must still broadcast globally, and channel/team scheme role updates must still reach that channel's/team's members, so clients refresh permissions live; dropping or user-scoping the event breaks this.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: server/channels/app/role.go:198-208 (built-in roles), server/channels/app/channel.go:1105-1116 (new channel-scheme role must be emitted), fix.diff:38-49

O6_input_shapes: custom role with no owning scheme -> global
team-scope scheme role -> one event per team using the scheme (paged)
channel-scope scheme role -> one event per channel using the scheme (paged)

O7_producer.where: Roles table/row mapping server/channels/store/sqlstore/role_store.go:384-423 and server/public/model/role.go:414-425 have no owning-scheme field at the pinned commit; SchemeStore has no reverse lookup by role name (server/channels/store/store.go:854-863)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: PatchScheme emitting role_updated/scheme event for the scheme's default roles via a direct Publish with empty broadcast
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer refreshing admin-console or client permission caches after a scheme rename/patch would plausibly copy the existing global role_updated publish pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: DeleteChannelScheme revert path publishing the reverted higher-scoped member/guest roles as role_updated with no channel scope
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The branch already reassigns memberRole/guestRole to higher-scoped roles that clients must re-fetch; emitting them directly beside the existing channel_scheme_updated publish is a natural addition.

O9_family: CWE-200 information exposure via over-broad websocket broadcast (missing audience scoping)
